reef.name: Lingcod & rockfish
reef.life_stage: Adult lingcod and recreationally targeted rockfish; rockfish species occupy different niches.
reef.habitat: Rock relief, connected rough ground and sand–reef edges are search leads. A high terrain score measures structure, not abundance.
reef.method: Sounder first, then a controlled bottom drift with your double-drop rig. For lingcod, investigate ledges and edges; for rockfish, also inspect suspended marks above the reef. Reset when bottom contact or boat control deteriorates.
reef.timing: Seasonal nesting and species movements can change use of the reef. Do not turn a spawning season into an assumed bite window.
reef.condition_response: Wind, chop and opposing seas reduce rig control. Surface radar/model currents help plan a test drift; the boat’s observed track and line angle determine the actual setup.
evidence_needed: Identified species, depth and fish marks on the day
Measured drift, rig weight and bottom-contact time
Comparable successful and empty drifts; survey method and effort
reef.search_for: Search mapped rock relief and rock–sediment boundaries; inspect both the bottom and schools suspended above it.
reef.presentation: Use a controlled bottom drift for lingcod, and adjust the rig to the depth of identified rockfish marks. Reset when line angle prevents effective contact.
reef.caution: Rockfish species have different niches and restrictions; a terrain grade is not a catch probability.
required_to_confirm: Identified species, depth and fish marks on the day
Measured drift, rig weight and bottom-contact time
Comparable successful and empty drifts; survey method and effort
reef.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

sheephead.name: California sheephead
sheephead.life_stage: Adults; identify juveniles and the sexually distinct adult forms.
sheephead.habitat: Rocky reef, kelp and benthic feeding habitat. Individual boulders and cavities require finer evidence than a general reef polygon.
sheephead.method: Use a controlled near-bottom bait presentation along a verified reef edge. Log legal-sized fish and unsuccessful drifts so apparent reef quality can be tested.
sheephead.timing: The rod-and-reel boat season is March–December in the reviewed 2026 rules; year-round diver/shore exceptions are different methods.
sheephead.condition_response: Bottom contact and room to reset safely matter more than an assumed lunar bite. Reduce scope if surge and kelp make rig control poor.
evidence_needed: Size and sex structure; legal identification
sheephead.depth_guidance: CDFW lists a broad 0–180 ft primary habitat range; this is not a local optimum or a guarantee that every patch is fishable.
sheephead.regional_notes: Appropriate at qualifying island and mainland reefs. Sheephead are part of the reef ecosystem; large males and juveniles are not interchangeable observations.
sheephead.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
sheephead.search_for: Search rocky reef with shelter and benthic prey, using mapped substrate to narrow a sonar search.
sheephead.presentation: Keep a bait near the reef with controlled gear, avoiding prolonged snagging and adjusting to the actual bottom.
sheephead.caution: Substrate classification does not resolve caves, individual rocks or prey abundance.
required_to_confirm: Size and sex structure; legal identification
sheephead.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

whitefish.name: Ocean whitefish
whitefish.life_stage: Fish feeding on or above bottom; avoid treating sonar height as seabed depth.
whitefish.habitat: Rocky and mixed substrate near island reefs and banks can support whitefish. The historical island assessment also describes use above softer bottom.
whitefish.method: Check sonar above the reef edge and vary a controlled bait presentation through marked fish. A double-drop rig is an operational option where legal and manageable.
whitefish.timing: Year-round legal season at all depths in the reviewed rules does not imply year-round presence on a particular reef.
whitefish.condition_response: Judge drift by the rig and marks. Strong flow can lift gear away from fish even when the surface looks calm.
whitefish.depth_guidance: The broad agency primary range extends to 300 ft; the current bottom-fishing limit still governs displayed candidates.
whitefish.regional_notes: A particularly relevant island/bank target, but historic regional abundance statements are not current site rankings.
whitefish.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
whitefish.search_for: Inspect rock–sand transitions and the water immediately above the seabed.
whitefish.presentation: Use a small bait presentation near observed marks and maintain reliable depth control; avoid assuming fish are tight to the highest rock.
whitefish.caution: Depth and habitat preferences vary; not every sediment polygon is equally useful.
whitefish.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

kelp-bass.name: Kelp bass / calico bass
kelp-bass.life_stage: Adult recreational targets; juvenile shelter/prey use differs.
kelp-bass.habitat: Persistent shallow reef combined with current kelp and bait observations. Canopy is seasonal and does not precisely trace the bottom reef.
kelp-bass.method: Search an accessible kelp or reef edge with cast or bait presentations appropriate to the observed fish. Keep safe reset room and log effort on comparable edges.
kelp-bass.timing: CDFW describes a long spawning season peaking in summer; spawning evidence is not a calibrated bite forecast.
kelp-bass.condition_response: Evaluate surge, kelp entanglement and boat control, not wind alone. No universal tide stage or current speed is assigned.
evidence_needed: Kelp observation date and native reef map
kelp-bass.depth_guidance: CDFW describes common recreational fishing on shallow reefs/kelp to about 70 ft, within a wider biological depth range.
kelp-bass.regional_notes: Useful on suitable Channel Islands and mainland habitat. Warm/cool differences and canopy loss mean one island cannot stand in for another.

source_links.title: CDFW kelp bass enhanced status report, 2019

kelp-bass.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
kelp-bass.search_for: Look for living kelp edges and rocky cover; confirm that old mapped canopy still exists.
kelp-bass.presentation: Work a bait, soft plastic or jig alongside cover while maintaining room to maneuver. Keep presentations near the structure rather than making long blind drifts.
kelp-bass.caution: Historical canopy is habitat context, not proof of present kelp or fish.
required_to_confirm: Kelp observation date and native reef map
kelp-bass.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

sand-bass.name: Barred sand bass
sand-bass.life_stage: Adult fish; juvenile eelgrass records remain nursery evidence.
sand-bass.habitat: Connected soft-bottom areas near structure, with seasonal schools that may extend away from the hard edge.
sand-bass.method: Use a search area across confirmed sand and nearby reef; compare short drifts and bait observations before favoring a particular edge.
sand-bass.timing: Summer/early-autumn aggregations appear in agency life-history accounts. Concentrations can change quickly and aggregation catch rates can overstate wider abundance.
sand-bass.condition_response: Favor controllable near-bottom presentation. Tide predictions do not identify when a local channel or shelf current will slack.
evidence_needed: Sediment area and hard-edge survey coverage
sand-bass.depth_guidance: The CDFW primary range is broadly 0–120 ft; no claim is made that deeper is better or that the study’s edge distance is universal.
sand-bass.regional_notes: Mainland shelf sand/structure is the main mapping context. Do not promote every Channel Islands rocky patch as equivalent sand-bass habitat.

source_links.title: CDFW barred sand bass life history

sand-bass.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
sand-bass.search_for: Search sand near reef transitions and bait schools; do not treat every island reef as sand-bass habitat.
sand-bass.presentation: Work a near-bottom bait or lure across the sand edge, keeping a repeatable presentation and logging empty passes as well as catches.
sand-bass.caution: Spawning-season aggregations can distort historical catch reports; more pressure is not proof of better fishing.
required_to_confirm: Sediment area and hard-edge survey coverage
sand-bass.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

spotted-bass.name: Spotted sand bass / bay bass
spotted-bass.life_stage: Bay/estuary populations; adult and nursery observations are separate.
spotted-bass.habitat: Bay and estuary soft bottom with eelgrass or accessible structure, not a generic offshore island reef.
spotted-bass.method: Select lawful bay areas, check local channels and restrictions, and fish presentations at the actual marked depth. Do not place a drift across vessel traffic.
spotted-bass.timing: Seasonal activity varies locally. Bay-specific observations are needed before any bite timing is scored.
spotted-bass.condition_response: Use observed channel flow, wind and visibility; ocean tide height alone does not provide local current speed or slack.
spotted-bass.depth_guidance: Local bay bathymetry and access govern; an offshore 200-ft ceiling is not a habitat model.
spotted-bass.regional_notes: Mainland bays such as San Diego/Mission/Newport are ecological context, not automatic fishing clearance. No island reef is promoted for this species without site evidence.

source_links.title: CDFW spotted sand bass management and habitat context

spotted-bass.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
spotted-bass.search_for: Focus on suitable bays, eelgrass margins and soft-bottom structure south of Santa Monica, not exposed Channel Islands reefs.
spotted-bass.presentation: Make short bait or lure presentations along actual vegetation and structure edges, adjusting to the observed tidal flow.
spotted-bass.caution: Bay habitat geometry is not yet available in this release; no offshore reef is substituted.
spotted-bass.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.life_stage: Coastal fish targeted by recreational anglers; nursery and trawl samples are distinct evidence.
halibut.habitat: Work connected sediment habitat and its edges. The current map’s shallow sediment areas are research candidates, not confirmed concentrations.
halibut.method: Search an area with a controlled drift and a presentation near the seabed. Use the sounder to check the edge and bait; move between comparable depth bands when an area produces no evidence.
halibut.timing: CDFW describes shallow spawning movements, but the calendar cannot locate fish. Local prey, visibility and present conditions remain important.
halibut.condition_response: Enough movement to cover ground can help searching, but excessive drift makes near-bottom presentation difficult. No universal current-speed optimum is assigned.
evidence_needed: Actual bait and fish observations at depth
Catch per fishing hour, including zero-catch attempts
halibut.search_for: Start on mapped shallow sand or mud, especially where bait occurs near a bottom transition.
halibut.presentation: Keep bait or a lure near the bottom on a controlled drift; change depth or location when bait and bottom contact are absent.
halibut.caution: Bottom temperature and current are not measured by the surface layer; confirm the actual depth with sonar.
required_to_confirm: Actual bait and fish observations at depth
Catch per fishing hour, including zero-catch attempts
halibut.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

white-seabass.name: White seabass
white-seabass.life_stage: Mobile adults; juvenile nursery records are not adult schools.
white-seabass.habitat: Kelp margins, rocky headlands and open-water feeding areas. A reef or squid report is a search clue only while it remains relevant and dated.
white-seabass.method: Check fresh bait and fish marks, then choose lawful live-bait, cast or other rod presentations at the observed depth. Do not drift blindly from a historical fleet dot.
white-seabass.timing: Year-round permission has a reduced one-fish limit March 15–June 15 south of Point Conception; presence changes with movement and forage.
white-seabass.condition_response: The method needs stable boat control and a manageable return. A calm surface and favorable moon do not supply a catch probability.
evidence_needed: Dated identified schools and actual depth
white-seabass.depth_guidance: Use fish/forage depth; the seabed may be much deeper. Retain vessel and method limits instead of treating every school as a bottom-fishing target.
white-seabass.regional_notes: Historic CDFW island fishing descriptions support regional habitat context only. Giant/black seabass is a different, protected fish.

source_links.title: CDFW white seabass FMP biological background

white-seabass.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
white-seabass.search_for: Inspect kelp margins and adjacent soft-bottom forage areas for squid or schooling bait.
white-seabass.presentation: Use an appropriately sized bait or lure at the observed fish depth; work quietly and use short repeatable passes instead of assuming every kelp bed holds fish.
white-seabass.caution: A historical kelp or sand polygon cannot confirm a squid spawn or a current seabass school.
required_to_confirm: Dated identified schools and actual depth
white-seabass.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

yellowtail.name: California yellowtail
yellowtail.life_stage: Mobile fish with age-dependent behavior; current species name Seriola dorsalis.
yellowtail.habitat: Island/reef edges, banks and offshore water with forage. Floating kelp and schools move; fixed bathymetric landmarks organize a search only.
yellowtail.method: Use recent bait, birds and sonar to select a rod-and-reel presentation; record the observed fish depth and whether schools were actually identified.
yellowtail.timing: California availability varies with seasonal migration and ocean conditions; warm water alone cannot establish an active school.
yellowtail.condition_response: Review the exposed transit and return as well as fishing control. Do not confuse a bank’s current-facing side with a modeled exact drift.
evidence_needed: Source timestamp, positional accuracy and fish depth
yellowtail.depth_guidance: A water-column target; bottom depth does not describe school depth or allow a deep bottom-fishing recommendation.
yellowtail.regional_notes: Channel Islands references must distinguish island side and exposure. San Clemente/San Nicolas access checks and the international boundary are separate from fish evidence.
yellowtail.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
yellowtail.search_for: Start at mapped island reef and kelp edges, then look for sardine, anchovy, mackerel or squid schools in the adjacent water column.
yellowtail.presentation: When fish are near the surface, present a lively bait or a casting jig; when marks are deep, take bait or a vertical jig to their depth. Make a short test pass before committing to a drift.
yellowtail.caution: No universal temperature, moon phase or tide height guarantees yellowtail. Bait and identified fish marks are the decisive missing evidence.
required_to_confirm: Source timestamp, positional accuracy and fish depth
yellowtail.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

bonito.name: Pacific bonito
bonito.life_stage: Schooling Pacific bonito; identify species and size, not just surface activity.
bonito.habitat: Coastal, island and offshore upper-water forage schools, which can move away from bottom structure.
bonito.method: Search active bait/birds and identified marks using a lawful cast, bait or trolling presentation. Keep an observation’s age visible.
bonito.timing: Historical seasonal/temperature associations do not define a present optimum or permanent hot spot.
bonito.condition_response: Keep boat control and other vessels in view during fast-moving schools; judge the return independently.
evidence_needed: Identified fish, school depth and bait
bonito.depth_guidance: Fish depth and presentation matter; seabed depth is not a bonito habitat cutoff.
bonito.regional_notes: Do not transfer Atlantic bonito assumptions. Northern Pacific form records support broad Southern California context, not an exact island point.
bonito.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
bonito.search_for: Search coastal and island water for feeding birds, bait and identified upper-water schools.
bonito.presentation: Cast to active schools, present bait, or use a lawful trolling presentation to locate feeding fish; follow confirmed marks rather than a fixed pin.
bonito.caution: Warm water and surface activity alone do not identify bonito.
required_to_confirm: Identified fish, school depth and bait
bonito.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

barracuda.name: California barracuda
barracuda.life_stage: Sphyraena argentea; do not substitute tropical great-barracuda ecology.
barracuda.habitat: Mobile coastal and island upper-water schools following small fish.
barracuda.method: Use identified forage/school observations and suitable rod presentations. Check nearshore wire/metal leader restrictions before choosing tackle.
barracuda.timing: Historical warm-season catch concentration is background, not a live bite calendar.
barracuda.condition_response: Evaluate safe cast/troll space and full-route seas. No bottom-current optimum is inferred.
barracuda.depth_guidance: The presentation follows school depth; no bottom-depth quality bonus is assigned.
barracuda.regional_notes: Relevant on mainland and island forage grounds when observed. Fish aboard can impose additional line/hook restrictions when switching targets.
barracuda.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
barracuda.search_for: Look for coastal forage concentrations and identify the fish before targeting surface activity.
barracuda.presentation: Use a bait or casting lure through identified schools; adjust presentation depth to marks and leave unproductive water.
barracuda.caution: There is no measured local bait-density layer or calibrated barracuda temperature optimum.
barracuda.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

bluefin.name: Pacific bluefin tuna
bluefin.life_stage: Mobile fish with size-dependent behavior and depth use.
bluefin.habitat: Schools can move quickly and occupy different depths. A single SST band is not a universal optimum.
bluefin.method: Treat offshore sectors as search references; use fresh school and bait evidence, appropriate equipment and lawful technique. Actual sonar marks should guide presentation depth.
bluefin.timing: Dated sightings can lose value rapidly. A past fleet track or landing count does not establish a current school.
bluefin.condition_response: Use the full trip exposure and return forecast. Surface-current products cannot predict a school’s movement or a deep jig’s drift.
evidence_needed: Recent identified school locations and observation method
Search effort and outcomes, not only successful reports
bluefin.search_for: Inspect ocean water transitions together with recent identified tuna and bait observations; check multiple depths.
bluefin.presentation: Use sonar and current school depth to choose live bait, a casting or vertical jig, or trolling. Match tackle to the fish size rather than the mapped water temperature.
bluefin.caution: A broad temperature range is not a bluefin bite curve; a surface map can miss deep schools.
required_to_confirm: Recent identified school locations and observation method
Search effort and outcomes, not only successful reports
bluefin.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

yellowfin.name: Yellowfin tuna
yellowfin.life_stage: Mobile pelagic fish; life stage and size affect depth and behavior.
yellowfin.habitat: Warm-water offshore schools with mobile forage; current fronts and floating material can organize a search.
yellowfin.method: Check recent quality-screened ocean context, then seek identified fish and bait with suitable rod gear. Plan fuel reserve and return exposure before committing to an offshore search.
yellowfin.timing: Migration varies seasonally and annually. An old catch report, high dock total or a moon phase cannot locate today’s school.
yellowfin.condition_response: Score the entire outbound–search–return window. Surface-current products cannot predict a fish’s path or the drift of a deep jig.
evidence_needed: Recent identified schools, depth and observation method
Cloud/quality-screened SST/fronts with native pixel size
yellowfin.depth_guidance: Separate presentation depth from seabed depth. The 200-ft bottom limit is not offshore range authorization or a pelagic habitat boundary.
yellowfin.regional_notes: A Southern California seasonal target whose availability changes among years. Tropical stock-wide habitat ranges cannot be turned into a local perfect temperature.

source_links.title: NOAA Yellowfin tuna biology and habitat

yellowfin.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
yellowfin.search_for: Use warm offshore water as broad context, then require bait, birds or identified schools to focus the search.
yellowfin.presentation: Search with lawful trolling or present bait and casting lures at confirmed schools. Check whether the water transition and forage persist as you move.
yellowfin.caution: A species-wide thermal reference is not a Southern California optimum or a fish-presence boundary.
required_to_confirm: Recent identified schools, depth and observation method
Cloud/quality-screened SST/fronts with native pixel size
yellowfin.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
yellowfin.thermal_note: No local numeric optimum is imposed; confirm forage and fish rather than excluding colder water.

dorado.name: Dorado / mahi-mahi
dorado.life_stage: Mobile pelagic fish; life stage and size affect depth and behavior.
dorado.habitat: Warm upper-water habitat and dated floating kelp/debris observations; neither a paddy nor a front guarantees fish.
dorado.method: Check recent quality-screened ocean context, then seek identified fish and bait with suitable rod gear. Plan fuel reserve and return exposure before committing to an offshore search.
dorado.timing: Migration varies seasonally and annually. An old catch report, high dock total or a moon phase cannot locate today’s school.
dorado.condition_response: Score the entire outbound–search–return window. Surface-current products cannot predict a fish’s path or the drift of a deep jig.
evidence_needed: Recent identified schools, depth and observation method
Cloud/quality-screened SST/fronts with native pixel size
dorado.depth_guidance: Separate presentation depth from seabed depth. The 200-ft bottom limit is not offshore range authorization or a pelagic habitat boundary.
dorado.regional_notes: Moving paddies need timestamps and observed positions. Artificially fixed paddy dots or old AIS stopping points are not habitat surveys.

source_links.title: NOAA Dorado / mahi-mahi biology and habitat

dorado.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
dorado.search_for: Look for warm offshore water and actual floating kelp or debris with associated bait.
dorado.presentation: Approach observed floating structure without crowding it, then present bait or a lure to identified fish. Record the time because the structure drifts.
dorado.caution: No current paddy detections are available; a forecast cell is not a paddy location.
required_to_confirm: Recent identified schools, depth and observation method
Cloud/quality-screened SST/fronts with native pixel size

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.life_stage: Surface-oriented fish encountered by West Coast troll fisheries; size and behavior vary.
albacore.habitat: Recent fronts and water masses can narrow an offshore search. Clouds, coarse pixels and stale imagery weaken the inference.
albacore.method: Compare recent SST, chlorophyll and current context, then look for actual bait, birds or fish. Start a search sector only after a fuel, range and return-weather plan; a colored front is not a catch location.
albacore.timing: Migrations change through the season and among years. Do not keep a fixed offshore hotspot alive after its supporting observation ages out.
albacore.condition_response: Longer exposure and a deteriorating return matter for the Parker. The comfort view and ensemble uncertainty apply to the complete travel window, not just the troll.
evidence_needed: Dated, cloud-screened fronts with native pixel size
Independent bait/fish sightings and catch effort
Fuel and range plan for the observed sea state
albacore.search_for: Prioritize ocean fronts and water transitions as search context for surface-oriented juveniles; look for forage and identified fish.
albacore.presentation: Use a searching troll or present bait at confirmed activity; compare both sides of a water transition rather than committing to a temperature number.
albacore.caution: Adult deep-water habitat and juvenile surface fisheries are different; fronts alone cannot confirm albacore.
required_to_confirm: Dated, cloud-screened fronts with native pixel size
Independent bait/fish sightings and catch effort
Fuel and range plan for the observed sea state
albacore.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
albacore.thermal_note: Broad juvenile eastern-Pacific tagged-fish envelope from the reviewed HMS synthesis, not an optimum.

lobster.name: California spiny lobster
lobster.life_stage: Legal-sized adult target; juvenile habitat alone cannot establish a productive hoop area.
lobster.habitat: Rocky shelter and kelp habitat with accessible edges. A reef outline is a search area, not a measured den or a legal-size lobster count.
lobster.method: From the Parker use lawful hoop nets, or separately planned hand collection by divers. Rods, traps, snares and tickle sticks are not lobster methods. Keep a gauge ready and log catch per lift/soak, including empty sets.
lobster.timing: The next scheduled opening is October 2, 2026 at 6 p.m. Pacific, through March 17, 2027, subject to current restrictions. The opener is time-specific, not all day.
lobster.condition_response: Darkness, kelp snagging, surge, vertical lines, boat control and retrieval matter. Tide height does not predict bottom current or a lobster catch window.
evidence_needed: Surveyed reef edge, depth and retrieval room
Legal-size catch per lift, soak and bait
lobster.depth_guidance: Use site-specific retrieval and method limits. Off Anacapa nets/traps are prohibited shallower than 20 ft; deep water is not inherently better and a 200-ft limit does not authorize diving.
lobster.regional_notes: Channel Islands MPAs and method-specific exceptions are complex; this app excludes all mapped MPAs from targets. West Anacapa’s pelican closure also restricts access January–October.
lobster.habitat_confidence: Moderate at habitat-class scale; site occupancy and legal-size catch are unverified.
lobster.search_for: Look for mapped rocky habitat and verify shelter and accessible adjacent ground before setting lawful hoop gear.
lobster.presentation: Plan the actual evening or night window, sound the bottom and assess wind, swell and line handling before setting gear.
lobster.caution: Daytime comfort is not a night-operation or diving assessment; old rock polygons do not locate dens.
required_to_confirm: Surveyed reef edge, depth and retrieval room
Legal-size catch per lift, soak and bait
lobster.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.life_stage: Ocean-feeding fish; species and stock identification affect legal access.
salmon.habitat: Mobile forage and water-column habitat matter more than a fixed reef pin. Coastal search sectors are geographic references.
salmon.method: Check the current local season, then use lawful gear to search observed bait and fish marks at their actual depth. Separate trolling presentation depth from seabed depth.
salmon.timing: Run timing and prey vary among years. Old landing reports or a moon phase do not establish today’s school position.
salmon.condition_response: Evaluate the outbound and return sea directions, trolling control and fog. Temperature or chlorophyll can guide a search only when recent, quality-screened and supported by forage evidence.
salmon.search_for: Use recent legal-season forage and identified fish observations to choose coastal feeding water.
salmon.presentation: Use lawful trolling gear at observed bait and fish depth, checking the entire transit and return forecast.
salmon.caution: No fixed reef or modeled surface temperature establishes an active salmon school.
salmon.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.life_stage: Adult-sized crabs; juvenile nursery habitat cannot be treated as a harvest hotspot.
dungeness.habitat: Broad, depth-qualified sediment areas are starting hypotheses. Crab distribution, predation, molt, bait and gear all affect results.
dungeness.method: When the season and chosen gear are permitted, compare a small number of sediment locations with consistent bait, gear and soak effort. Record empty sets as well as catches. Check bottom type and retrieval conditions before setting.
dungeness.timing: Season permission, health restrictions and trap permission are checked separately. Molt and local movement may change availability.
dungeness.condition_response: Longer/deeper sets increase handling, buoy-line and retrieval demands. The user’s 200-ft ceiling stays in force. A deeper comparison requires new depth-qualified habitat, lawful gear and a suitable retrieval plan.
evidence_needed: Catch per trap-hour or hoop set by depth
Bait, soak time, size, sex and empty sets
Direct evidence of local predation; a poor catch alone cannot identify sea otters as the cause
dungeness.search_for: Search mapped sand and mud in a legal area and season, comparing depth and soak effort systematically.
dungeness.presentation: Use lawful crab gear suited to the actual depth and retrieve safely; log soak duration, bait, depth and empty sets.
dungeness.caution: Neither sea-otter presence nor deeper water alone establishes productive crab grounds.
required_to_confirm: Catch per trap-hour or hoop set by depth
Bait, soak time, size, sex and empty sets
Direct evidence of local predation; a poor catch alone cannot identify sea otters as the cause
dungeness.tactics_basis: Practical search and presentation guidance synthesized from the linked ecology; not a calibrated catch model.
